newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold little changed as focus remains on PGMs.
newsitem.headline: Gold little changed as focus remains on PGMs.

text.p: Gold was little changed versus the London close in early Europe as the market watched and waited to see what platinum group metals (PGMs) would do next.
Gold was quoted in early business here at $344.10/$344.50 an ounce versus $344.00/$344.50 at the London close on Monday.
Silver was also lower at $4.76/$4.78 versus $4.82/$4.84.
Platinum remained below peaks around $500.00 seen in recent sessions, after drifting lower on Monday, but it nonetheless was slightly higher here compared with London's close.

Platinum traded at $470.00/$475.00 versus $464.00/$469.00 at the London close. Traders believed it was too soon to say whether prices of either platinum or palladium were ready to break their recent uptrend.
At least one Swiss-based trader believed that Russian deliveries of PGMs to Japan may continue to be delayed well into the summer, possibly until late July or early August.
Russia sounded more optimistic however about chances for beginning deliveries.
Earlier on Tuesday in Moscow, a Russian finance ministry spokesman said the state precious metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport should receive an export licence this week.
But one Swiss-based trader remained sceptical, saying markets believed in-fighting among Russia's bureacracy was a major reason for delays in signing export agreements.

He added that forward rates remained extremely tight for both palladium and platinum. Forward rates were quoted at 300 percent, and 150 percent respectively earlier this week on a few scattered trades, he said.
